findings.text: Per process helpers and operation tables with external linkage include ownership computation, inode eviction, inode creation, attribute handling, liveness driven dentry handling, directory emission and link handling for reuse across proc implementation.
Sequential file helpers for rcu list iteration by position and for allocation and binding of private iteration context have external linkage.
Per task command name file supports open with single entry sequential handling, sequential read and seek, custom write handling and single release.

Command name update accepts bounded user bytes, signals user memory fault and missing task distinctly, allows only writers from the same thread group to change the name and emit a connector event while rejecting others as invalid, and always releases the looked up task.
Command name display resolves the task from the stored inode, signals missing task, emits the current name followed by a line break through sequential output, and releases the task.
Executable link resolution shares the task executable path with an added reference when such a file exists and releases the temporary file reference, otherwise it signals absence.

Per task link resolution acquires the task signal exec update lock in killable read form before permission validation and handler dispatch and releases that lock and the task reference on every exit path.
Common task link lookup propagates task absence, interrupted lock acquisition and denied credentialed access without invoking the inode specific handler.
Proc inode accessor returns the directory entry pointer held in the proc specific inode extension.
Directory entry use check succeeds only while the usage count remains nonnegative, using atomic conditional increment semantics.
Generic proc link handling rejects entries no longer in use as invalid, otherwise registers a delayed release for the entry and returns its stored target.
Per process link inodes provide readlink and follow link behaviour with attribute change disallowed.
Follow link handling rejects missing dentries, delegates to the common task resolver, transfers successful paths to lookup continuation and encodes failures as error pointers.
Readlink handling starts from denied access, resolves through the common task path, formats that path into caller memory with length capping and releases path references.
Path formatting uses a bounded kernel staging buffer, reports allocation failure and user memory fault distinctly and truncates output to caller length.

Ownership derivation assigns global root to kernel threads, otherwise starts from effective credentials under read side protection and, except for fully accessible process directories, falls back to namespace root when dumpable state is not owner restricted, with further fallback to global root when namespace mapping is invalid.
Pid tracker list insertion for new base directory inodes and removal during eviction of directory inodes are both serialized by the pid spinlock using rcu list operations.
Eviction cleanup detaches the tracker node only for directory inodes.

Per task inode creation provides a new inode with unique number and current time, default operations, an associated pid reference from the task, derived ownership and security state, and clean failure on allocation or pid lookup error.
Base directory inode creation extends generic per task construction by registering the result on the pid tracker for later flushing.

Attribute handling fills generic values, defaults ownership to global root, reports absence for pids invisible in the caller namespace so that listing and stat agree, and otherwise refreshes ownership from live task state under read side protection.
Inode refresh recomputes ownership from current task state, clears set identity mode bits and reapplies task derived security state.
Dentry revalidation under read side protection succeeds only while an inode remains attached and its pid still maps to a live task, refreshing ownership on success.
Liveness test checks whether the pid retains any task association, and the dentry delete hook uses that test to request immediate reclaim for dead tasks.
Per process dentries install revalidate and delete handlers that implement live task retention.
Directory emission tolerates already present, absent and concurrently created children, best effort derives inode number and type when available, and always attempts emission of the requested name.

Map file name parsing accepts only two hexadecimal address values separated by one dash with strict termination, rejects leading zero variants and overflow and unrepresentable values, and outputs the numeric range on success.

Map file revalidation declines rcu lookup mode, holds a task reference and credential checked memory reference, uses killable mmap read protection only around the exact mapping existence test and releases all references.
Map file dentry remains valid only when the encoded range matches a current mapping exactly, refreshing ownership and security from the task on success.
Mapped file dentries combine exact mapping revalidation with immediate reclaim for dead tasks.

Mapped file link resolution parses the dentry name as an address range and shares the user visible path of the mapped file only when the exact mapping exists and has backing storage, under killable mmap read protection.
Collected mapping descriptor holds start address and end address with file access mode for deferred instantiation after locks are released.
Mapped file follow link handling requires checkpoint restore capability in the initial user namespace and otherwise follows the generic per task path.
Mapped file link inodes provide readlink and capability gated follow link behaviour with attribute change disallowed.

Mapped file instantiation creates a link inode with user permission bits derived from mapped file readability and writability, binds mapped file link handling and operations, assigns a small fixed size and splices as unmountable with mapped file dentry handling.
Unmountable splice marks the dentry as not mountable and aliases it to the given inode with caller supplied dentry handling.

Mapped file lookup rejects unknown tasks and malformed names, requires credential checked memory access, searches for an exact mapping under killable protection and instantiates only when backing storage is present.
Mapped file directories provide lookup with descriptor permission checks and disallow attribute change.

Mapped file directory iteration emits dot entries first, snapshots file backed mappings under read protection into a growable collection, releases protection, then instantiates hexadecimal range names while advancing directory position.
Mapped file iteration reports missing task, treats tasks without memory as empty, and propagates interruption and allocation and access failures.
Mapped file directories provide generic read and seek with shared iteration.
Timer listing context retains a pid reference and namespace for translation plus a transient task reference filled during iteration.
Timer listing acquires a task reference at start under read side protection, walks the signal timer list by position, and on stop drops the task reference and leaves the protected region.
Each timer entry reports identifier and signal details with notification kind and target scope and translated pid and clock identity, skipping entries that became invalid while held under timer lock.
Timer listing open allocates private context and records the target pid and namespace for later iteration.
Timer listing files provide open with private context, sequential read and seek and private release.
Rcu list start returns the node at the requested offset from the head or null when beyond the end.
Rcu list iteration advances the position counter and follows the next link, restarting from the head when given the start token.
Sequential private open allocates zeroed context of caller requested size, binds it to the sequential handle on success and cleans up on allocation or setup failure.
Ownership derivation and attribute handling and dentry revalidation and timer list walking all execute under rcu read protection with matching release.
Exact mapping existence checks and mapped file path extraction all hold mmap read protection in killable form with matching release.
Timer entry display holds the timer lock with interrupt protection while validating and formatting.
Overlength command name input is silently truncated to capacity while still reporting the original length, so callers cannot detect truncation from the return value.
Strict rejection of leading zeros and overflow in range names prevents distinct address ranges from aliasing to the same textual name.
Task and memory and path and pid references acquired during link and mapping operations must be released on every exit to avoid leaks.
Mapped file directory collection uses a snapshot phase under protection followed by an emission phase without protection to avoid faulting while holding the mapping lock.
Command name storage accepts at most one less than task name capacity to preserve termination.
Mapped file names encode start dash end in hexadecimal within a buffer sized for two address words plus separator and terminator.
Mapped file link size is fixed at sixty four bytes.
Readlink staging uses a kernel buffer sized by the system path maximum.
